A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Img-Diff work. Their main text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLaVA and MGM fine-tuning experiments, benchmark results, filtering ablations, and a human assessment of generated data.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds InternVL2 evaluations, alternative-dataset comparisons, data-scaling experiments, and lexicon and CoCoT studies.

M1.justification: The SDXL image generation, Difference Area Generator, and two-stage captioning pipeline remain unchanged. Section 11 adds an alternative object-replacement procedure that samples same-category nouns from a WordNet-derived lexicon instead of relying on LLM-selected replacements.

E1.justification: V3 actually uses CLEVR-Change's synthetic geometric scenes as alternative training data in Section 9.2; v1 only discussed that dataset. The three image-difference benchmarks, eight general MLLM benchmarks, and object-replacement/removal tasks remain.

E2.justification: V3 adds direct comparisons against CLEVR-Change augmentation and combined Spot-the-Diff/Image-Edit-Request augmentation, plus InternVL2-FT controls. Figure 5 removes Bing Chat and Bard, and the object-removal comparisons drop MGM. These substantially revise comparator membership beyond simply adding benchmark results.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include matched second-fine-tuning controls for InternVL2, 1B/13B models, expanded-data and 8,930-sample lexicon conditions, and CoCoT prompting on MMVP. Existing benchmark metrics and two-epoch benchmark-specific tuning remain. The additional caption-source dataset is inconsistently sized at 34,538 versus 34,583 samples.

E4.justification: V3 adds analyses of dataset expansion, lexicon substitution, contrastive prompting, and transfer across model sizes. The filtering study moves from Section 4.6 to Section 14, but its no-BITM-filter condition is removed. The MGM object-removal analysis is also removed; it is not merely relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the same 1,000-sample human quality assessment with voting; additional result tables do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original LLaVA-7B/MGM-7B main comparison scores remain. V3 adds extensive results, including InternVL2-8B MMVP scores of 38.7 for FT and 43.3 with RP, and 31.3 for LLaVA under expanded-data training. It removes MGM's object-removal MMVP result of 37.3 versus 50.7 with replacement alone. New CoCoT results have condition labels inconsistent with the accompanying prose.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs. The cosine-similarity and IoU reasoning remains unchanged; the new discussion of dataset size concerns empirical trends rather than a mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The central claim that regional image-difference data improves fine-grained recognition is retained. V3 explicitly emphasizes automatic scalability and extends the contribution statement to InternVL2. Its abstract and conclusion omit v1's comparison with models trained on much larger datasets.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning diminishing returns from more data, lexicon-driven diversity, and transfer across model sizes. It removes v1's warning that object-removal augmentation can harm MGM and its conditional applicability argument, while adding a limitation concerning poor inpainting quality.

D1.justification: V3 adds frozen/trainable-parameter explanations, WordNet lexicon construction instructions, and resource estimates: four A100 GPUs, 4.5 days for image generation, and roughly two days for filtering/captioning. Existing model choices, filtering thresholds, image concatenation, and code/data access information are largely retained.

R1.justification: Section 9 and Table 4 substantially expand positioning against existing datasets through automation, object-domain coverage, and regional annotation comparisons. New references include InternVL2, CoCoT, MagicBrush, MJ-Bench, and multimodal contrastive-learning work. This goes beyond bibliography renumbering or citation additions alone.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the main prose are rewritten around the synthesis methodology. Main-text ablations move to the supplement, Section 6 becomes a supplementary-material roadmap, and Appendices A-C become reorganized Sections 15-17 within a separately introduced supplement.

P2.justification: V3 redraws and condenses Figure 2, restructures wide benchmark tables into metric blocks, and replaces explicit score deltas with arrows. It adds a visual dataset-comparison table, numerous experimental tables, and object-removal examples. The original diversity table is replaced by prose, with extensive relocation and reformatting of retained displays.

improvement.justification: Direct alternative-dataset comparisons and validation across additional model families and sizes strengthen evidence for the central object-replacement method beyond v1's two 7B-model experiments. Added resource details also help reproducibility. The net improvement is limited by removal of negative MGM object-removal evidence and inconsistencies in CoCoT labels and dataset counts, which weaken completeness and reporting reliability.
